page: Microsoft Azure D4_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity sits at 16.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and includes no bundled local storage, requiring remote Azure storage options for operational disks.

Instruction set features for the D4_v4 include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI variants), AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. In empirical benchmarks, single-threaded execution displays average performance, scoring 1435.59 in stress-ng and 1215.0 in Geekbench single-core, aided by single-threaded gzip compression at 24.08 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core and aggregate bandwidth metrics trend into the bottom 25% of evaluated cloud servers. The Geekbench multi-core score reached 2726.0, while PassMark returned a total CPU score of 4444.4. Memory bandwidth evaluates at 26.1 GB/sec for uncached read-only workloads and 21.2 GB/sec for writes.

Application and system benchmarks reflect the constraints of its two physical cores and low memory bandwidth. Database operations under PassMark scored 1430.16, with Redis SET throughput achieving 3.58 million operations per second. Static web serving yielded 3.9 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scored 17.39 GB/sec, settling in the bottom 10%. Small language model execution (135M parameters) achieved 239.46 tokens per second during prompt ingestion and 98.14 tokens per second during generation.

Cost efficiency is aligned with standard general-purpose commodity compute profiles. The lack of onboard local storage limits scratch disk I/O performance unless coupled with managed network disks. The instance fits mid-tier microservices, web app backends, general-purpose enterprise application testing, and lightweight background processing tasks that do not saturate multi-core compute or depend on high sequential memory bandwidth.
description: Microsoft Azure D4_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Operating on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz with hyper-threading over 2 physical cores, it supports AVX-512 instruction sets but provides no onboard local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate balanced single-core throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1215.0 and 24.08 GB/sec gzip compression. However, multi-core and memory subsystem metrics fall into lower percentiles, with PassMark CPU scoring 4444.4 and uncached memory reads measuring 26.1 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 3.58 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.9 GB/sec static web serving. The D4_v4 serves workloads such as standard web services, development staging environments, small-scale caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
